definition: Oracle's procedural extension to SQL, used for blocks, stored routines, and triggers.
example: A developer defines a stored routine that validates a row before saving it.

definition: PostgreSQL's procedural language for implementing server-side functions and triggers.
example: A developer writes a trigger function that records a timestamp.

definition: A human language used in oral and written communication.
example: An editor reviews a Polish exhibition guide.

definition: A human language with multiple regional standards used in speech and writing.
example: A localization team chooses the appropriate Portuguese standard for its interface.

definition: A programming language for describing text and graphics on a printed or rendered page.
example: A print workflow positions vector shapes on a page before printing.

definition: A low-code formula language used in Microsoft's Power Platform.
example: A developer uses a formula to filter records shown in a gallery.

definition: A shell and scripting language that passes structured objects through pipelines.
example: An administrator filters a list of running processes by memory usage.

definition: A logic programming language that answers queries using facts, rules, unification, and search.
example: A developer queries a family relation derived from recorded parent facts.

definition: A human language used in spoken and written communication with multiple writing conventions.
example: A publisher specifies Gurmukhi for a Punjabi edition.

definition: A statically typed, purely functional programming language that commonly compiles to JavaScript.
example: A developer represents an optional form field with an explicit type.

definition: A general-purpose programming language with dynamic typing and an extensive standard library.
example: An analyst reads a CSV file and summarizes counts by category.

definition: A programming language designed to express quantum operations and algorithms.
example: A developer prepares and measures a qubit in a simulator.

definition: A family of related human languages or varieties known collectively as Quechua.
example: An interpreter asks which Quechua variety a speaker uses.

definition: A programming language and environment for statistical computing and graphics.
example: A researcher fits a regression and plots its residuals.

definition: A Scheme-derived programming language and platform for building other languages.
example: A developer uses a macro to define notation for a tiny expression language.

definition: A human language used in speech and writing.
example: A translator checks a Romanian software manual.

definition: A dynamic, object-oriented programming language with support for blocks and iterators.
example: A developer groups records using a Ruby block.

definition: A human language normally written in the Cyrillic script.
example: An editor proofreads Russian captions for a video.

definition: A compiled systems language whose ownership and borrowing rules help enforce memory safety.
example: A developer passes a borrowed slice to a parser without copying its contents.

definition: A human language also known as Yakut.
example: A teacher records a Sakha pronunciation exercise.

definition: A human language used for spoken and written communication.
example: A translator reviews a Samoan visitor guide.

definition: A human language used in spoken and written communication.
example: An interpreter explains an appointment notice in Sango.

definition: A human language that can be written in Ol Chiki and other scripts.
example: An editor reviews a Santali reading lesson in Ol Chiki.

definition: A human language used for oral and written communication.
example: A broadcaster prepares a Saraiki public announcement.

definition: A text-generation language for parameterizing and generating SAS code.
example: An analyst uses a macro parameter to generate the same report for several years.

definition: A programming language and software environment for managing data and conducting statistical analyses.
example: An analyst summarizes survey responses with a SAS procedure.
sense_note: Clarify language versus the larger platform if needed.

definition: A stylesheet language that compiles to CSS and supports variables, modules, and reusable rules.
example: A developer uses a mixin to share a typography rule across components.

definition: A statically typed language combining object-oriented and functional programming.
example: A developer maps a transformation over an immutable collection.

definition: A Lisp dialect characterized by lexical scope and first-class procedures.
example: A student passes a comparison procedure into a sorting function.

definition: A block-based programming language used to build interactive projects.
example: A learner connects an event block to movement blocks for a sprite.

definition: A broad language label that can group Bosnian, Croatian, Montenegrin, and Serbian standards.
example: A cataloger records the specific standard for each edition rather than merging titles.
sense_note: Use specific standards where the distinction matters.

definition: An XML-based specification for exchanging provisioning requests between systems.
example: An identity client sends a standardized request to create a user record.

definition: A human language also known as Southern Sotho.
example: An editor reviews a Sesotho version of a community bulletin.

definition: A human language used for spoken and written communication.
example: A teacher prepares a Shan reading exercise.

definition: Writing command sequences for execution by a shell interpreter.
example: An operator uses a shell script to count files in each directory.
sense_note: Specify shell when the syntax matters.

definition: A human language used in speech and writing.
example: A reviewer edits Shona subtitles for a training video.

sense_note: Confirm the intended language sense, especially whether the label refers to the Slavic variety or a historical German one.

definition: An early object-oriented programming language designed in part for simulation.
example: A programmer represents each customer in a queue simulation as an object.

definition: A human language with more than one writing convention.
example: A publisher specifies the script for a Sindhi edition.

definition: A human language written in the Sinhala script.
example: A translator reviews Sinhala instructions on a public kiosk.
